/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 29 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3178 (-90)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5103 (-248)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2390 (-12)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1797 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1013 (1)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market extended its losses today, with the BCI 182 5TC falling a further $2,249 to close at $46,278. Weakness was evident across both basins, although growing tonnage availability continued to weigh particularly on sentiment in the Pacific. In the Atlantic, the C8 transatlantic round voyage slipped below the $60,000 mark, falling to $59,563 while the C9 fronthaul route declined by $2,706 to $87,183. Fresh activity remained relatively limited so far this week. Despite a few fixtures surfacing from the Brazil region, the C3 index fell below the $40 mark to $39.718 today. In the Pacific, two miners remained active, taking a few vessels at the $13.70-$13.75 level. The resulting pressure pushed the C5 index down a further $0.61 to $13.725.

Atlantic
There was talk of Arcelormittal’s 150,000/10 Port Cartier to Qingdao with second half October loading fixing at $48 but the details could not be confirmed. Maran Eagle (209,388 2021) was linked for a 190,000/10 Nouadhibou to Qingdao cargo basis 14/23 October at $41.50 last night.

Asia
Rio Tinto fixed 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao for 15/17 October at $13.70. BHP was rumoured to have fixed 160,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao over the same loading window at a similar level. Last night, Vale fixed a TBN for 180,000/10 TRMT to Dung Quat 7/9 October at a rate in the mid/low $6s.
PANAMAX
Today saw another session of mixed opinion regarding the direction of both the trans-Atlantic and fronthaul markets. Some brokers indicated that activity was largely position-driven, with NC South America highlighted as the busier region. As a result, tonnage open in the West Mediterranean is reported to have attracted increased attention. The Canola Zibo (80,801 2020) open Gibraltar 30 September was reported to have fixed a trans-Atlantic round via Puerto Drummond at $25,000 to Mercuria with some suggesting the fixture does not include EU ETS costs. Market sources also noted an improvement in Atlantic demand, with the US Gulf said to be showing greater levels of activity, providing some support to sentiment. Overall, however, participants suggested that market fundamentals remain relatively well balanced for the time being. The Yasa Sapphire (82,406 2023) open Krishnapatnam 28 September fixed an EC South America fronthaul at around $25,000 to Cofco. Meanwhile, the ASL Galaxy (81,056 2016) that sailed Haldia on 15 September fixed for a similar fronthaul trip, but the rate was reported. By comparison, sentiment in the Pacific has continued to soften, with confidence in the market also said to be slipping. Demand from Indonesia is described as subdued, while Australian export activity, which was cited last week as a key factor underpinning rates, is also reported to have eased. As a result, market participants generally characterised the Pacific as coming under increased pressure. The P5TC fell by $113 to conclude at $21,507.
SUPRAMAX
Another modest gain as the 11TC average rose $90 to $22,710 today. The US Gulf ended its recent decline with an injection of fresh demand, with both the fronthaul and transatlantic routes now hovering around $33,000. The Mediterranean continues to lack enough business to support the tonnage there, partly due to the new risk area, whilst the Continent remains very firm driven by scrap and Russian stems. The South Atlantic appeared well balanced with transatlantic numbers still edging up. Asia has another week of disruption with Coaltrans and the upcoming Golden week in China, but rates remain steady, driven by the backhaul market and continued volume from South East Asia. This has helped maintain period interest with the GLBS Hero (63,742 2024) open Cebu fixed for 5 to 7 months (intended first leg North Vietnam to NC South America) at something in the low $23,000’s.

Atlantic
The New Joyful (64,691 2022) open New Orleans 10-11 October went on subjects for a trip India intention petcoke at $37,000 basis redelivery WC India or $38,000 basis EC India with Oldendorff. A 56,000-dwt was said to have fixed from the US Gulf for a trip WC South America with grains at $27,000, but no further details emerged, and the Lorenzo (61,250 2016) open Caribbean early October was on subjects basis delivery Sao Luis for a trip East Mediterranean at $36,000 to Bunge.

Asia
The Ocean Brave (63,226 2020) Subic Bay early October went on subjects to Norden for a trip via Indonesia back to the Philippines in the high $23,000’s and the Crane (57,809 2010) Hazira early October was apparently on subjects for a trip via Salalah to WC India at $16,000. From South Africa, Ultrabulk fixed the Ocean North (64,595 2026) Durban 11-14 October basis delivery Port Elizabeth for a trip Far East intention manganese ore in the mid $26,000’s plus mid $260,000's ballast bonus.
HANDYSIZE
The market delivered a mixed performance today, with some regions holding steady while others recorded modest gains. The BHSI edged up by 1 point to 1,013, while the 7TC average rose by just $18 to $18,226. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only marginal adjustments were observed, with rates remaining healthy. Views in the South Atlantic and US Gulf were mixed: some participants noted that charterers were increasing their bids and owners were showing greater resilience, while others reported fewer fixtures and lower rate levels being discussed on certain trading legs. The Bona (32,844 2012) was placed on subjects by Norden for a trip from Upriver to North Brazil at $26,000, although further details were not disclosed. Asian markets were more subdued, as reduced cargo enquiry and softer activity contributed to a mild downward drift in rates.

Market Fundamentals
India Directs Coal-based Power Plants to Run at Full Capacity
India’s Power ministry directed around 112 coal-based power plants with capacity of 50 MW or higher, including Tata power’s 4.00 GW Mundra plant, to run at full capacity until the end of 2026, McCloskey reports. The decision came as a result of a sharp decline in coal stocks at the 183 operating power plants monitored by the Central Electricity Authority, where coal inventories declined for 23 consecutive weeks, down 52% year-on-year to 22.7 Mt, as reported by McCloskey based on CEA data. The decline followed higher electricity demand and lower renewable and hydro availability amid curtailed monsoon rainfall.
